questions.q:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The volunteers completed its community service projects ahead of schedule.
questions.s:
The part that contains the error is 'its'. The word "its" is a possessive determiner used for inanimate objects or animals. However, the sentence refers to the volunteers, who are people, not inanimate objects or animals. Therefore, the sentence should use a pronoun that refers to people, such as 'their,' to properly attribute the completion of community service projects to the volunteers. Additionally, the plural 'their' matches with the plural 'volunteers'. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: The volunteers completed their community service projects ahead of schedule.

NOTE:

Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books."

questions.q:

The mango is the ______ fruit.
questions.s:
The sentence implies a superlative quality of the mango compared to other fruits. The superlative form of the adjective "sweet" is "sweetest," indicating the mango is the most sweet among all fruits. "Sweetly" is an adverb, "sweet" is the base adjective, and "sweeter" is comparative, none of which fit the superlative context.

Thus, "sweetest" is the correct choice.

The complete sentence is: "The mango is the sweetest fruit."

The correct sentence would be: "She has the sweetest and most melodious voice among all the singers."

questions.q:
Select the correct degree of comparison for the given sentence.

My new work is challenging and interesting.
o: My new work is most challenging and interesting.
My new work is more challenging and more interesting.
My new work is challenge and interesting.
My new work is most challenging and most interesting.
questions.s:
Here the correct answer is My new work is more challenging and more interesting.

Key Points

  • The correct degree of comparison for the given sentence is option 2: "My new work is more challenging and more interesting."
  • The sentence compares two qualities of the speaker's new work - it is both challenging and interesting as compared to his/her previous work. When comparing two qualities, we use the comparative degree of adjectives, which is formed by adding "-er" to the end of the adjective, or by using the word "more" before the adjective.
  • In this case, we cannot use the superlative degree of adjectives, which is formed by adding "-est" to the end of the adjective or by using the word "most" before the adjective, because there is no third quality to compare with.
  • Example sentences:
    • This book is more interesting than the last one I read.
    • Running is more challenging than walking.
    • Sarah's essay was more well-written than John's.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 2.


Correct Sentence: My new work is more challenging and more interesting.
